issues.description: The problem statement requires that the function 'start_app' must be the global entry point, but the template declares 'global main' and provides a 'main' label. The solution file defines a 'start_app' label but does not declare it global (it still has 'global main'). This mismatch between the required global entry symbol and the symbols declared in the template and solution will confuse students and may prevent the intended entrypoint behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the entrypoint consistent: declare 'start_app' as the global symbol in the template and solution (replace 'global main' with 'global start_app'), and ensure a 'start_app' label is present and implemented. Alternatively, update the problem statement to require 'main' as the global entrypoint if that was intended. Ensure both template and solution use the same global label to match the specification.

issues.description: The problem statement requires the function 'start_app' to be the global entry point, but the template defines 'global main' and a 'main' label. The solution file contains a 'start_app' label that is not declared global and still includes 'main'. This mismatch of the program entry-point identifier across artifacts will confuse students trying to map the requirement to the provided code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the entry-point identifier consistent with the problem statement. For example, in helloWorld.asm (template) replace 'global main' with 'global start_app' and rename the 'main:' label to 'start_app:'. In the solution, ensure 'start_app' is declared global (add or change to 'global start_app') and remove or align any remaining 'main' label so all artifacts use the same entry-point name.
